newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Nam Fong offers 340 mln shrs at HK$2.88.
newsitem.headline: HK's Nam Fong offers 340 mln shrs at HK$2.88.

text.p: Property investment and development concern Nam Fong International Holdings Ltd said on Monday it was offering 340 million new shares at HK$2.88 each.
It said 272 million shares will be subscribed by way of a placement and the balance of 68 million shares will be offered for public subscription in Hong Kong.

After the capitalisation of loans of about HK$151 million to Guangdong Investment Ltd and expenses, net proceeds of about HK$788 million will be raised from the share offer by the Hong Kong-based firm, which has its property business in China.
The firm has market capitalisation of about HK$3.92 billion at a prospective weighted average price earnings multiple of 5.76 times and pro-forma fully diluted price earnings of 7.20 times.
It forecast a combined profit after tax and minority interests before extraordinary items of not less than HK$520 million for the year ending December 31.
The share issue will run from November 26 to 29. Dealing in shares in Hong Kong is expected to start on December 9.
Jardine Fleming Securities is the global coordinator, sponsor and lead manager of the share offer.
Nam Fong currently holds 10 development and two investment properties and rights to manage and lease two additional properties in southern China's Guangdong province.
The 10 development projects have a total gross floor area of about 13.45 million square feet and a total capital value attributable to the group of about HK$8.89 billion as at August 31, 1996.
Nam Fong said HK$484 million of the proceeds will be used for the expenditure of and investments in its development projects, with the balance used as general working capital.
It said Guangdong Investment would hold about four percent of its enlarged share capital after the new issue.
Nam Fong's properties, comprising residential and retail complexes, are located mainly in Guangzhou and other major cities in Guangdong province.

"We believe that the PRC (People's Republic of China) economy will continue to grow in the coming years. The standard of living of people in large cities, particularly in Guangzhou, will continue to improve," chairman Wong Wah said in a statement.
"This should lead to higher levels of consumer spending and hence increase the demand of quality retail property in prime locations with good transportation links," he added.

"We believe that with more overseas Chinese investing in the PRC and local PRC residents having higher income levels, the demand for quality residential housing in good areas is forecast to escalate," he said.
